A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of SGLT2 inhibitors for the prevention of cardiovascular events in patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, and for the treatment of heart failure in patients with and without diabetes, is a major advance for the field of cardiology and endocrinology.
SGLT2 inhibitors are now the preferred first-line therapy for most patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, and should be used as early as possible in the course of diabetes.

The main takeaway from our work is that
SGLT2 inhibitors are an important class of drugs for the prevention of cardiovascular events in high-risk individuals, including those with type 2 diabetic kidney disease.

SGLT2 inhibitors are a promising new class of glucose-lowing medications with the potential to reduce the risk of heart failure among patients with type diabetes mellitus and atherosclerotie cardiovascular disease.

SGLT2 inhibitors should be considered as a treatment option for patients with heart failure, especially those with reduced ejection fraction, and for patients with type 1 and type 2 diabetes who are at risk for heart failure.
